body.statement: Apply the published rank-two deterministic count certificate to the canonical anchor hypergraph. For generic factor rows, over all laws \(P\in\mathcal M\) whose cohort loading-mean vector ranges over \(\mathfrak M_{\lambda}(H)\), every coordinate of \(\mu(P)\) is a functional of the entire observed law \(P_O\) if and only if \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). The forward causal transport constructs the functional in \(\operatorname{def:counterfactual-functional}\). When \(r_{1,2}(H_3)<T-2\), there exist \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\), with loading means in their corresponding admissible classes, such that \(P_{0,O}=P_{1,O}\) as complete observed-record laws and \(\mu(P_0)\ne\mu(P_1)\).
body.justification: The contribution is the causal transport from a published generic count certificate to an entire-observed-law functional and, on failure, to observationally identical panel laws with different missing means.
body.gap: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak already supply the rank-two count criterion, and Streinu and Theran supply pebble machinery; neither constructs cohort-specific loading and error laws that agree on the complete observed causal-panel distribution while changing a missing mean.
body.consumer: The certificate determines when Lei and Ross's \(\operatorname{apm}\) workflow and Liu, Wang, and Xu's counterfactual-imputation workflow can report every untreated cohort-time mean under a rank-two specification.
